emergency.general: Call 112 for all emergencies — it's the universal number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance services. Operators generally speak English and Croatian. You can also call 192 for police, 193 for fire, or 194 for ambulance directly. In tourist coastal areas, English-speaking assistance is readily available.

healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Croatia. Emergency numbers (112/194/192/193), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance, and vaccination recommendations for travelers.

medications.generalAdvice: Croatia follows EU/Schengen regulations for medication imports since joining the Schengen area in 2023. EU prescriptions are accepted, while non-EU prescriptions may need verification from a local doctor. For controlled substances, carry a Schengen medical certificate. Croatia's HALMED (Agency for Medicinal Products) oversees pharmaceutical regulation.

controlledSubstances.note: Cannabis is illegal for recreational use in Croatia. Medical cannabis is limited to specific conditions with Croatian prescription only. CBD products with 0% THC are legal. Do not bring any THC-containing products.
Controlled under Croatian narcotics law. Requires Schengen certificate or doctor's letter. Carry only personal-use quantities in original packaging.
Controlled substances. Requires documentation and Schengen certificate. Contact Croatian health authorities or your embassy if you need to bring ADHD medications.
Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry Schengen certificate, doctor's letter, and original prescription. Customs may inspect quantities.
Croatia has comprehensive legislation banning new psychoactive substances. Possession and import are criminal offenses.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Croatian or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry prescriptions and a multilingual medical certificate.
medications.generalAdvice: Croatia, as an EU member state, follows Schengen medication import rules. Non-EU travelers may bring up to 3 months' personal supply of prescribed medications in original packaging with a doctor's certificate. For narcotic and psychotropic substances, a Schengen certificate validated by your national health authority is required. Croatia strictly enforces drug laws — carrying undocumented controlled substances can lead to criminal prosecution.

cultural.tipping: 10% at restaurants appreciated. Round up for taxis.
cultural.dressCode: Casual on coast. Cover shoulders/knees in churches. Comfortable shoes in Old Towns.
cultural.greetings: Handshake formal. Kiss on both cheeks between friends. 'Bok' is casual hello.
taboos: Being loud in Old Towns at night
Not trying local wine when offered

safety.lgbtSafety: Croatia has made progress on LGBTQ+ rights as an EU member, with life partnerships legally recognized. Zagreb Pride is well-established. However, conservative attitudes persist, especially outside Zagreb and the coast — public displays of affection between same-sex couples may attract stares in smaller towns.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Croatia is very safe for solo female travelers. The Dalmatian coast, Zagreb, and islands are well-traveled and welcoming. Standard precautions apply at night in cities — stick to well-lit areas and use reputable transport.
safety.notes: Croatia is one of the safest countries in Southern Europe for tourists. Violent crime is very rare. Petty theft can occur in crowded tourist areas along the coast during peak summer season. Landmine remnants from the 1990s war exist in some rural and border areas — stay on marked paths in these regions.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen, joined 2023). UK, EU, Australia, Canada also visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-June and September (warm, fewer crowds). July-August peak in Dubrovnik.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured

Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties

Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
